children: The Indian rupee opened 7 paise higher at 95.89 per dollar on September 16, compared with Tuesday’s close of 95.96, as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s rate decision later in the day amid continued pressure from elevated oil prices.

According to Finrex, the Indian rupee is expected to open at 95.91 per dollar on September 16, with the dollar index at 99.70 and Brent crude at around $108.15 per barrel. The Indian basket has remained above $128 per barrel, keeping pressure on the rupee as oil companies step up dollar purchases and foreign portfolio investors continue to exit equities and bonds.
Exporters are likely to hedge their forward 1-2 month exposures, while importers may continue buying on dips, with RBI dollar sales providing some relief, it added.

Asian currencies were mostly weaker against the US dollar, with the South Korean won declining 0.53% to lead losses. The Japanese yen and Indonesian rupiah slipped 0.14% each, while the Taiwan dollar, Thai baht, Singapore dollar and Chinese renminbi also weakened. The Philippines peso and Malaysian ringgit bucked the trend, gaining 0.16% and 0.02%, respectively.

The dollar was hanging on to recent gains on Wednesday and trading near multi-week highs on a handful of major peers ahead of a Federal Reserve decision where traders expect the first of what could be several U.S. interest rate hikes.

title: Currency Check: Rupee opens 7 paise higher at 95.89/$ ahead of Fed rate decision
